title: 5 Myths About Brela With a Dog: What's Actually True
metaDescription: Brela has a dog beach at Stomarica, but dogs are barred from most other beaches. Rules on ferries, heat, fees, vets and the EU pet passport, for 2027.
content:
## Myth 1: "Brela has dog beaches everywhere"

Brela has one official dog beach: **Stomarica (Plaža za pse)**, a small pebble-and-rock beach on the north side of the resort. Its main drawback is that shade is limited, so a dog-safe umbrella or tarp is worth packing. It sits next to a café stand, and several apartments are within a few hundred metres of it. Some listings mention additional dog-friendly spots, such as the pine-fringed Vruja cove, but Stomarica is the only one confirmed as a marked dog beach.

The myth falls apart at the main beaches. Across the Makarska Riviera, resort beaches generally restrict pets during the bathing season. That includes the famous Punta Rata, the beach with the Brela Rock. Dogs are not welcome on the busy bathing stretches, and signs are enforced.

**Better move:** Base yourself near Stomarica, swim early, and keep the dog on a leash on the coastal path. Outside the season, quiet pebble coves are easier to use, but check for signs.

## Myth 2: "Dogs are welcome in the old town and in every restaurant"

Brela has no walled old town. It is a string of small settlements along a pine-lined waterfront, with a promenade that works well for walks. Croatia expects dogs to be on a leash in all public spaces, including promenades and parks, unless a sign says otherwise. Muzzles are not required on streets, but they are required on ferries.

Restaurants make their own rules. Terraces are usually fine, interiors usually are not, and food-serving areas are the most likely to be refused. Insider perspective: asking before sitting down is standard practice, and a polite question settles it in seconds.

**Better move:** Eat on terraces, bring a collapsible water bowl, and keep a mat for the dog.

## Myth 3: "Ferries are easy, and catamarans are the same thing"

On Jadrolinija car ferries, dogs travel on the open deck and must be leashed and muzzled; larger dogs cannot go into the indoor lounges. Small pets under 8 kg are the exception and can sit in a carrier on a lap or under a seat.

Catamarans are the weak point. Dogs over 8 kg need a reserved deck box for an extra fee, and the booking is made by email with a Jadrolinija sales office. The fee is not published as a flat price. Some travellers report that the box service is not reliably available. Insider perspective: if the plan is Hvar or Brač with a large dog, the car ferry from Makarska or Split is the realistic route.

**Better move:** Book early, ask by email, and have a fallback that uses a car ferry.

## Myth 4: "Pet-friendly means free"

Fees are modest but not universal. Some Brela apartments take dogs of any size for no extra fee, and others charge around €5 per pet per night. Hotels in the Bluesun group are described as pet-friendly, and typically add a fee. The catch is availability: only about 13–17% of Brela rentals accept pets, so the good ones near Stomarica go first.

**Better move:** Book months ahead, confirm the fee and any size limit in writing, and ask whether a garden or terrace is included.

## Myth 5: "Summer is fine because there is a sea"

Pebble beaches in July and August get hot enough to burn paws, and midday temperatures are dangerous for dogs. **May, June and September** are the best months: sea temperatures are comfortable, the beaches are quieter, and trails along the coast are walkable in the morning.

## Vet basics and EU pet passport rules

A microchip is mandatory for all dogs in Croatia. Dogs entering from other EU countries need an EU pet passport, a valid rabies vaccination, and an ISO microchip. A new EU regulation, 2026/131, replaced the old one on 22 April 2026, but the rules for travellers are almost unchanged and existing passports stay valid. The minimum age for entry is 15 weeks because of the rabies vaccination timing. Dogs coming from outside the EU need a health certificate instead of a passport. Up to five animals per owner can travel on a non-commercial basis.

For a clinic, the nearest larger options are in Makarska, so save a vet's number before arriving. Bring tick and flea prevention, because the pine belt is a tick habitat.

## What matters most for a dog owner choosing Brela

Three things decide the trip: the accommodation must be confirmed as pet-friendly, the dates should be outside July and August, and the plan should not depend on a catamaran. Brela suits a calm dog and an owner who is happy with one dog beach, shaded walks and terrace dining.

**Verdict:** Brela is moderately dog-friendly. It is good for walking, with an official dog beach, a fair number of welcoming apartments and an easy base for car trips. It is not suited to owners who want every beach open to their dog or who plan island hopping with a large dog. A rating of 3.5 out of 5 fits.

faq.question: But isn't Brela famous for dog beaches?
faq.answer: It has one confirmed official dog beach, Stomarica. Other listings mention a second or third dog-friendly spot, such as Vruja, but the main bathing beaches, including Punta Rata, restrict dogs during the season.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed on ferries in Croatia?
faq.answer: Yes. On Jadrolinija car ferries dogs travel on the open deck with a leash and muzzle. On catamarans, only pets under 8 kg in a carrier may travel in the salon, and larger dogs need a pre-booked deck box.

faq.question: Does a dog cost extra in Brela accommodation?
faq.answer: Often, but not always. Some apartments charge no fee and others about €5 per dog per night. Only a minority of rentals accept pets, so confirm the policy before booking.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to enter Croatia?
faq.answer: An ISO microchip, a valid rabies vaccination and an EU pet passport or an equivalent health certificate. The minimum age is 15 weeks. The updated EU regulation of April 2026 left the rules mostly unchanged.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Brela with a dog?
faq.answer: May, June and September. July and August bring dangerous afternoon heat and hot pebbles, and the dog beach has little shade.

faq.question: Do dogs need a muzzle in Croatia?
faq.answer: On ferries, yes, except for assistance dogs. On streets and promenades a leash is required, and muzzle rules depend on the venue or transport operator.

quickAnswer: The usual assumption is that Brela is a dog paradise because it has a "plaža za pse". It has one dog beach, Stomarica, and little else. Most other beaches stay off-limits in summer, large dogs are hard to take on catamarans, and July heat is risky. Brela works best for dogs in May, June and September.
